question: Is 0.3.0 fit to stay the current release for a long time: do large KV pools load with MTP, is the KQ-mask change byte for byte the same, and does a long mixed workload stay up without memory growth?
machine: GMKtec EVO-X2 class, Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (gfx1151), 128 GB, 96 GB carve
model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS, MTP draft head IQ4_XS

draft_ubatch.what: tools/manager.py draft_ubatch(pool): 2048 up to 524288 cells, then 2048*524288/pool in steps of 256, never under 512 (STRIX_SPEC_DRAFT_UBATCH)
draft_ubatch.why: the MTP draft context reserves a dense mask over the whole KV pool for its ubatch (~4.8 KiB a cell at 2048): 3.9 GB at 768K cells, which failed to allocate after the target and its K/V had loaded (a user's log, 2026-09-26)

loads_4_slots_mtp_after_an_8K_prompt_gb.columns: dedicated GB, shared GB, draft ubatch

draft_ubatch.note: dedicated GPU memory tops out near 92 GB of the 96 GB carve; beyond it the display driver places allocations in shared memory (loads, slower)
draft_ubatch.users_case_768K_q8_0_mtp: tmp/ragged/multi_deep_probe.py --evict --restore: E 50.6 s, A/B/C first tokens 74.8 / 50.1 / 78.6 s, D 2386 tokens 3.8 s, E + 3.9K tail from disk 4.7 s, F 837 tokens 1.8 s; no error

kq_mask_seq_bits.what: set_input_kq_mask gathers the membership bits of a ubatch's sequences (2-16, one cell array, windows >= 4096 cells) in one pass, two bytes a cell; each first row tests those instead of the 32-byte bitsets
kq_mask_seq_bits.check: STRIX_KQ_MASK_CHECK=1 fills every mask the upstream way as well and compares byte for byte: 4 conversations of ~28K tokens (128+ masks), images in several conversations (256+), eight agents (512+): 0 differ

inputs_ms_4_conversations_112K_cells.unit: median host time of a 12-token step's inputs (STRIX_DECODE_TIMING), 74-76 steps
